description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

dailyInsight.headline: Audit which configuration layer gets to broker a Codex credential
dailyInsight.insight: If you are evaluating a Codex main-branch build that includes its new network-proxy credential broker, audit the configuration layers before enabling it: a project configuration should not be able to select the broker or replace its provider context, while a trusted layer should have a deliberate policy for sandboxed and escalated commands.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The fresh public Codex commit adds a credential-broker setting, sanitizes broker and provider-context values out of project configuration when trusted broker configuration exists, carries trusted context into filtered shell environments, and restores brokered credentials in the explicit unsandboxed escalation path. Its end-to-end zsh-fork test checks that the real fixture GitHub token does not appear in sandboxed output.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A repository is a collaborative work surface, while credential policy is a trust decision. Separating them can make an agent workflow easier to reason about, but the source is implementation and tests rather than a release guarantee or evidence that every provider and deployment shares the boundary.

actions.audience: Maintainer or security owner evaluating a Codex build with network-proxy credential brokering
actions.label: Trace the credential decision across configuration layers
actions.instruction: In a disposable test setup, map the user, managed, thread, and project configuration layers that can reach Codex. Verify that project-controlled configuration cannot enable the broker or replace provider-context variables, then run one harmless sandboxed command and one separately approved escalation-path check without placing a real secret in repository files.

receipts.title: Add credential brokering to network proxy feature config
receipts.supports: Shows the public implementation and tests for trusted broker configuration, project-config sanitization, filtered shell context, and the explicit unsandboxed escalation path.

receipts.title: Codex pull request #40466
receipts.supports: Shows the merged main-branch change description and its stated coverage of configuration layering, project protection, shell snapshots, Windows handling, escalation, and an end-to-end GitHub credential-broker test.

confidence.basis: The merged public commit, its configuration and runtime diff, and its stated end-to-end test agree on the intended boundary. The call remains an audit rather than an adoption recommendation because the sources do not establish a release, default enablement, or behavior in a particular environment.

dailyInsight.limitation: The receipts do not establish that the feature is released or enabled by default, that a given Codex installation includes it, or that every credential provider, operating system, shell, extension, and escalation path has equivalent protection.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise or withdraw this call if public configuration documentation or a regression shows that project files can still enable the broker or replace trusted provider context, that a sandboxed command receives the real test credential, or that the escalation path restores credentials outside its explicit trust transition.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for released configuration guidance that names supported broker providers, configuration precedence, and observable behavior for sandboxed versus escalated commands.
